QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_54

question.text: A corporate treasurer needs to hedge a USD 15 million receivable due in 3 months using exchange-traded USDINR derivatives. Considering the domestic client-level position limit (higher of 6% of total OI or USD 20 million), the workbook USDINR ELM (0.50% for futures and 0.75% for options) and that currency derivatives are cash-settled in INR, which practical challenge should the treasurer anticipate?

answer.text: The USD 15 million hedge is within the applicable client limit and can be executed on the exchange, but the treasurer must arrange INR initial margin (including ELM of 0.50% for futures or 0.75% for options on the mark-to-market value of the gross open position) and manage daily MTM cash flows in INR, while the USD receivable arrives only at maturity — creating an interim cash-flow mismatch that must be funded
The USD 15 million position exceeds the client limit of USD 10 million per currency pair, requiring the hedge to be split across multiple brokers
The hedge cannot be executed on exchanges because corporate hedging requires RBI approval and is permitted only in the OTC market
The cash settlement in INR means the hedge will not provide any effective protection against USD/INR exchange rate movements

explanation.text: The Logic: USD 15 million is below the USD 20 million floor / 6%-of-OI client limit, so the hedge is permissible. The treasurer must, however, post INR margin (USDINR futures ELM is 0.50% on the MTM value of gross open position, options ELM 0.75%) along with SPAN/initial margin and 50% cash collateral, and meet daily MTM in INR. Since the USD receivable arrives only at maturity, interim INR margin and MTM cash needs create a cash-flow mismatch. The Trap: The client limit is not USD 10 million per pair. Corporates can hedge directly on exchanges (post 2008 liberalisation). Cash settlement in INR still provides effective economic hedging — the INR P&L offsets the USD receivable's INR-equivalent move. The ELM applicable to USDINR is the workbook 0.50% for futures and 0.75% for options on MTM value, not a generic 1%. Note: The interim daily MTM is the biggest operational challenge versus OTC forwards (where settlement is at maturity). Treasurers typically arrange working-capital lines to fund margin calls during the hedge's life.
